newsitem.title: FRANCE: French journalists' strike leaves news kiosks bare.
newsitem.headline: French journalists' strike leaves news kiosks bare.

text.p: A one-day strike by journalists in protest at government plans to scrap their tax privileges left newspaper kiosks bare on Wednesday, with only a handful of national and provincial newspapers available.
Of national dailies, only the left-leaning Liberation, the Communist l'Humanite and the horseracing journal Paris-Turf were published.

Unions said provincial journalists were among the strongest supporters of Tuesday's 24-hour strike over plans to scrap a 30 percent income tax deduction partly for professional expenses which journalists say is effectively part of their salary.
Regional newspapers, including Sud-Ouest, Le Republicain Lorrain and Le Dauphine Libere, did not come out on Wednesday.
In the Mediterranean port city of Marseille, the strike stopped publication of all three local dailies -- Le Provencal, Le Meridional and La Marseillaise.

Public broadcasters and news agencies were badly hit by the strike. The stoppage fired a warning shot across the centre-right government's bows as civil servants, teachers, rail and power workers prepared for a 24-hour strike on Thursday against cutbacks and record unemployment.
